verdict.strongest_covered_cluster: The core alert-to-response and mitigation-verification workflow is strongly covered: duplicate grouping, primary paging, acknowledgement and triage, false-alarm versus incident branching, record and owner creation, parallel coordination/status duties, mitigation, same-signal verification, and retry.
verdict.most_consequential_gap: The escalation path does not explicitly identify the alert manager as the actor that escalates to the secondary on-call engineer; the incident-record boundary for preserved timeline data is also only implicit.
verdict.coverage_summary: Weighted coverage is 35/38. Nearly the entire operational lifecycle is represented, including failure retry and learning follow-up. The high-confidence alert qualifier is absent, while alert-manager ownership of escalation and storage of the preserved timeline specifically in the incident record are partial. No absent or contradicted system-defining requirement triggers a cap.
